name: libdvbcsa
desc: Free implementation of the DVB Common Scrambling Algorithm
why: An open implementation of the DVB scrambling cipher, a window into how satellite and cable TV protection works.

brief.what_it_is: libdvbcsa is a C library that implements the DVB Common Scrambling Algorithm (DVB/CSA), the cipher used to scramble MPEG transport stream packets in digital satellite, cable and terrestrial TV. It provides both encryption and decryption. It takes MPEG-TS packets and a control word (key) in, and returns scrambled or descrambled packets out. It ships a single-packet implementation and a faster parallel bitslice implementation, and the homepage describes its API as five functions for the single-packet path and six for the bitslice path.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents it as a free, portable, GPL-licensed implementation of a standard cipher that is otherwise hard to get as open code. The author argues that since libdvbcsa implements a published standard, using it is legal, and that the GPL keeps it free and limits its use to free software products.
brief.how_it_works: The library offers a classic one-packet-at-a-time cipher path and a parallel bitslice path that processes several packets at once using MMX, SSE or Altivec SIMD instructions, which the homepage credits for throughput of 300 Mbps or more on recent processors. The homepage says it has been tested on 32-bit, 64-bit and 128-bit word widths and on both little-endian and big-endian machines. The homepage does not explain the internal cipher design beyond this.

commands_seen.context: Homepage's Git checkout instruction for getting the source. The leading # is part of the page's code block as shown, not a comment the user needs to type.

brief.install_notes: No build steps, dependencies or first-run configuration appear on the homepage or the repository page. The only install route shown is cloning the Git repository from code.videolan.org or downloading a release from the releases page. The brew formula was not checked and the brew caveats were empty. Use of the SIMD paths depends on the target CPU supporting MMX, SSE or Altivec.
brief.standout: It is a small, focused library for a cipher that most people only meet inside closed set-top boxes and conditional-access systems, and the author presents it as legal because it implements a published standard. Its two-tier design, with a simple scalar path and a SIMD bitslice path, is a clear example of performance work on a cipher.
brief.status: Maintained, with weak evidence. The homepage names 1.1.0 as the latest release but gives no date. The GitLab repository page shows it was created on January 12, 2017 and is under GPL-2.0-or-later, but it shows no last-commit or release date. The release date and recent commit activity could not be confirmed from the pages fetched.
brief.caveats: The 300 Mbps throughput figure and the portability claims are the author's own and were not independently checked. The legal statement is the author's view and is not legal advice. Other caveats are inferred from the page: the SIMD fast path depends on MMX, SSE or Altivec hardware, and the GPL restriction on use with free software only is part of the license terms the author describes. The homepage was reachable and the repository page loaded, but the README text itself was not visible in the repository fetch.
quotes: libdvbcsa is a free implementation of the DVB Common Scrambling Algorithm - DVB/CSA - with encryption and decryption capabilities.
Freedom. libdvbcsa is released under the General Public License, ensuring it will stay free, and used only for free software products.
Simplicity. The API comes with only 5 functions for the single packet implementation, and 6 functions for the parallel bit-slice implementation.
